sprint: A page carrying voice narration now says so on its own card. Voice MVP Ship 1 stored per-page narration at slide.metadata.narration = {ref, durationMs}, but there was no way to tell at a glance which pages had a clip — you had to open Personalize -> Add Something -> Voice on each page in turn. Both page strips now show a small 🔊 badge on any page whose narration.ref is set.
task:
WHERE THE HINT GOES, and three places it deliberately does not. The badge is DOM chrome over the thumbnail in both page strips — window.renderList (the sidebar #slideList .thumb cards) and window.renderTimeline (#timelineList .timeline-thumb cards) — driven by one shared _hasNarration(s) predicate so the two strips can never disagree about which pages carry a clip.

REJECTED THE CANVAS: Creator Governing Rule #5 (Publish Fidelity) means whatever the centre pane shows is exactly what Publish produces, so a badge drawn there would land in the published book, reel and strip.

REJECTED BAKING INTO s.thumbnail: narration is not a rendered property of the page. DOM chrome keeps thumbnails pure renders and avoids regenerating them.

REJECTED AN OBJECT STRIP ENTRY: narration is page-level, not an object. The Object Strip's two synthetic entries (Background, Artwork Place) each map to a real selection; narration has none.

pointer-events:none on the badge is load-bearing rather than tidy — the sidebar .thumb is itself both the click target (d.onclick = () => showSlide(i)) and the HTML5 drag handle wired by _wireSlideListDnD, so a badge that could receive a pointer would eat both. .timeline-thumb gained position:relative deliberately: it has overflow:hidden and no positioned children of its own, so establishing a containing block changes nothing else, and the badge is inset (right:3px, bottom:3px) so nothing clips.

REFRESH: js/contextPanel.js's _setNarration and _removeNarration now call a shared _refreshPageStrips(), which invokes window.renderList() and window.renderTimeline() through the try/typeof guard this codebase already uses at six other cross-module call sites (js/pageOps.js, js/projectManager.js, js/themeEngine.js, js/creationFlow.js x2, and inside contextPanel itself). host.markDirty() only flags the project dirty — it does not re-render — and PageRuntime.notify() would be wrong here, because it calls ContextPanel.refresh() and would rebuild the Voice panel out from under the flow the child is in.

TWO TEST-SIDE FIXES, both disclosed, neither an app bug, and no assertion weakened. The app code was correct throughout; both failures were false premises in my own assertions.
1. B3b/B5b failed with the timeline badge present in the DOM but offsetParent === null and 0x0. Grepping found <div class='timeline' hidden> at index.html:288 and nothing in js/ that ever un-hides it. Removing the attribute in the test before measuring was the first fix — and it was insufficient.
2. The same two still failed. Rather than guess, a throwaway diagnostic walked the ancestor chain and reported .timeline with hidden:false but display:"none" — so CSS was hiding it too. css/style.css:1280 is `.timeline{ display:none !important; }`, sitting immediately above the strip's own retained-but-unreachable styling at 1281. An author-stylesheet !important can only be beaten by an INLINE !important, so both checks now use wrap.style.setProperty('display','block','important') and restore afterward. The retirement check was strengthened, not dropped: it asserts BOTH halves (hasAttribute('hidden') && computed display === 'none').

FINDING WORTH RECORDING: the timeline strip is retired-but-maintained. It is hidden twice over and nothing in js/ revives it, yet renderTimeline() still runs and still builds its cards — which is why the badge is present in the DOM there at all. Both strips were badged anyway, so whichever one a future layout revives already carries the hint.

Verified 21/21, zero page errors, via voice_badge_verify.mjs (scratch-only) across eight sections: B1 no badge before narration in either strip and the page genuinely carrying none; B2 both badges appearing after a real WAV import through the native filechooser with NO manual renderList()/renderTimeline() call from the test, which is what proves _refreshPageStrips() is genuinely wired in; B3 rendered visibility, pointer-events, absolute positioning, glyph and title, plus the retirement finding; B4 monkeypatching window.showSlide and clicking the badged thumb still yielding showSlide(0); B5 the timeline badge sitting inside its own thumb with real size; B6 a second page via the real #addPageBtn with only page 1 badged in both strips; B7 Remove Voice clearing both badges with no manual re-render; B8 zero page errors.
